subject: harness: the provider you saved is the provider you get back
prompt:
The provider you saved is not the provider you get back. The setup wizard writes `[llm] defaultProvider` and `[llm.<id>] model` to config.toml (and a custom endpoint to secrets.json) and says "restart required" — but a new process ignores all of it. A profile saved as `custom` / `mock-small` opens on `google` / `gemini-2.5-flash`, with or without keys in the keychain or the environment. Two defects in the startup ladder in packages/orchestrator/src/bin/rune-cli.ts cause it:

- The config rung only honours a provider from a hand-written list of six built-in ids, and its credential check knows only env vars, `[llm.*].apiKey` and secrets.json — not the credential store. A saved `custom` provider, or any of the other registry presets, fails the gate and auto-detect answers instead with whatever key happens to be on the machine.
- When startup has to re-pick a model, it takes the built-in default for the provider or else the Google default, so any provider outside the six — `custom` above all — is handed `gemini-2.5-flash`, a model it does not serve.

Move the ladder into a pure, injectable module and fix both defects. Precedence does not change: CLI flags, then the sticky `/model` pick, then config.toml, then auto-detect.
- A saved provider (sticky or config) is usable when it is `custom` with a usable endpoint (a base URL in secrets.json; its key may be in the sidecar or the credential store), a local runtime (e.g. `ollama`, which needs no key), or ANY registry preset that has a credential from any store: the credential store, the preset's env var, `[llm.<id>].apiKey`, or a saved key. An unusable sticky pick falls through to config; an unusable config provider falls through to auto-detect.
- The model is `--model` when given; otherwise the sticky pick's own model for the sticky rung; otherwise `[llm.<id>] model` for any id; otherwise the CLI's built-in default for that provider, the preset's default model, or the custom endpoint's own model — never another provider's default.
- Auto-detect keeps today's behaviour: funded capacity first (an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` selects `anthropic` / `claude-sonnet-4-6`; an `OLLAMA_API_KEY` selects `ollama-turbo`), and `openrouter` as the last resort.
- The CLI uses the module.

Keep the existing exported APIs working, and keep the existing tests passing.

Interface the fix must provide — a new module `packages/orchestrator/src/startup-selection.ts` that exports:
- `StartupSelectionInput`: `{ cliProvider?: string; cliModel?: string; config: { llm: { defaultProvider?: string } & Record<string, unknown> }; secrets: { keys?: Record<string, string>; custom?: { baseUrl?: string; model?: string; key?: string } }; lastUsed?: { provider: string; model: string } | null; env?: Record<string, string | undefined>; hasStoredCredential: (id: string) => boolean; getPreset: (id: string) => { defaultModel?: string; envVar?: string; local?: boolean } | undefined }` (the `[llm.<id>]` sections sit inside `config.llm`, e.g. `config.llm.custom.model`).
- `resolveStartupSelection(input: StartupSelectionInput): { provider: string; model: string; source: "flag" | "sticky" | "config" | "auto" }`.
- `modelForProvider(provider: string, ctx: { config; secrets; getPreset; cliModel?: string }): string` — the model a provider opens on, by the rule above.
